$doc: MQ Research Gate — architecture & monetization atlas. Machine-readable source of truth for AI chats. Human view: docs/atlas.html. Feedback log: docs/feedback.json.

app.name: MQ Research Gate
app.oneLiner: A detective's study for the Qur'an: meaning is earned from within the text (the organic Qur'anic methodology). Notice a word, open a case on its root family, gather every place the Book uses it, form a hypothesis, then weigh the classical dictionaries.
app.stack: React + Vite + TypeScript SPA (app/) over a Hono + node:sqlite backend (server/). MCP server (mcp/) exposes corpus+research to an AI. Optional remote research channel (remote/) on Postgres + Better Auth. Electron desktop wrapper (electron/).

principle.core: Studying stays local, offline and free; the community is the paid, cloud layer.
principle.constraint: You can only enforceably charge for what the server holds, never for what already sits on the reader's disk (the app ships as local code + local SQLite).
principle.consequence: Monetization lives entirely on the cloud remote. The local app + both local databases + the MCP stay free.

components.name: App
components.role: Reader + investigation UI. Talks to the local server at /api/v1, and directly to the remote for the community layer.

components.name: Server
components.role: The ONLY thing that touches the local databases. Reads quran.db, reads+writes research.db. Serves /api/v1.

components.name: MCP
components.role: Lets an AI study the corpus + the reader's local research and propose notes/indications/board items (source='ai'). LOCAL and FREE. Reuses the server query layer.

components.name: Remote
components.role: Optional, invite-only cloud research channel. The paid surface: auth, roles, the claim spine, plan/entitlements, gated community reads + publishing. Separate service from the local server; shares only a login.

components.name: Desktop
components.role: Wraps the built SPA + server in a desktop window.

quran.db.location: local, ships with the app (~150 MB)
quran.db.holds: Qur'an text in four scripts, per-word morphology (root/lemma/form), roots, ~9 classical lexicons (Lane, Lisan, Maqayis, Mufradat, ...), translations, FTS indexes.
quran.db.corrections: Shipped as signed, versioned patch files applied in order (see CORPUS.md). The corpus is reference material, not research.
quran.db.onCloud: MOVING. Step 1 done: the data is copied into Postgres schema `corpus` (remote DATABASE_URL) and verified exact, row-for-row. Step 2 (not started): port the query layer so the app/MCP read Postgres. Until then the app and MCP still read quran.db.

postgres.command: npm run corpus:migrate   (add -- --verify to re-verify only)
postgres.firstRun: 294,804 rows, 143.5 MB, 18 s, exact; every table content-fingerprinted; view 77,915=77,915; FKs 9/9; indexes 29/29
postgres.collation: every text column COLLATE "C" (= SQLite BINARY). The DB default English_United States.1252 would re-sort Arabic; proven load-bearing — the هدي forms query returns identical ORDER only with C.
postgres.edition: corpus.corpus_meta mirrors the patch channel's keys (corpus_version, schema_version) + source_sha256

research.db.holds: cases + board layout, form_research (established meanings) + form_revisions, trails, notes, word_indications (+ refinements), user_root_meanings, motifs, compare_sets, settings. Plus own-outbox derived_submissions / derived_proposed_claims.
research.db.ownership: A one-row owner table (name, email, uuidv5-of-email) makes the file self-describing and portable.
research.db.aiWrites: MCP proposals are tagged source='ai' and stay proposals until the reader accepts them in the app.

monetization.model: Sell infrastructure + collaboration, not the Book. Free tier = local-first study (offline, no account). Paid tier = the cloud community: reading the group's readings and publishing to it.
monetization.roleMeaning: What you may DO in the research process. reader<researcher<moderator<maintainer. remote/src/roles.ts, requireRole(min).
monetization.planLadder: DATA, not code: table plan_tiers (name, rank, label), edited at runtime by a maintainer. Seeded free (0) < pro (100); e.g. add student (50), scholar (200). free is always rank 0; pro is the COMMUNITY tier and can't be removed.
monetization.planMeaning: What you have PAID for. Orthogonal to role — a tier may be called 'researcher' or 'admin', but administering is the maintainer ROLE. remote/src/plans.ts: meetsPlan(user, minTier, tiers), requirePlan(minTier, runner). Fails closed: unknown tier never passes; a lapsed plan counts as free.

gate.middleware: requirePlan('pro') runs AFTER requireRole on paid routes: role = 'are you allowed to', plan = 'have you paid for it'.
gate.activeFlag: planActive (paid AND high-enough rung AND not lapsed) — the app trusts this, never the plan name alone.

monetization.billing: Not wired yet. A maintainer grants a plan out of band: `npm run set-plan -w @alsiraat/remote -- email pro [days]` or POST /plan (maintainer). This is the single seam a real payment provider slots into with no rework of the gate.
monetization.enforcement: Real because the gated DATA lives on the cloud, not the client. A modified/offline client cannot obtain community readings or publish without an active plan.

communityLayer.before: The group's readings were PULLED and mirrored into local research.db derived_* tables so they worked offline — which also put them on the reader's disk forever, un-gateable.
communityLayer.after: Read LIVE from the remote, gated (requireRole + requirePlan), never stored locally. Offline/free/unpaid readers simply see their own work.

communityLayer.appConsumers: app/src/screens/Divergences.tsx (⚖ list) and the reader's indication chips via app/src/persistence/db.ts indications.forWord (merges remote community readings only when planActive).

phases.summary: plan ladder free<pro; requirePlan → 402; set-plan CLI + POST /plan; planActive on /me; migration 0005_entitlements.sql; 10 boundary tests.

phases.summary: POST /divergences + GET /community/readings (gated); derived_* mirror + pull path deleted; Divergences.tsx and indication chips read live; sync-boundary test adapted; pull.test removed.

phases.title: Publishing gated
phases.summary: requirePlan on POST /submissions and POST /claims; upgrade nudges in ShareButton + ProposeReading; review/establish stay role-only.

phases.title: MCP → cloud
phases.summary: Kept the MCP local & free. The original blocker — the cloud had none of the corpus — is being lifted by the corpus migration below (data is now in Postgres; the query layer isn't ported yet). The second blocker still stands: moving personal research to the cloud breaks the AI-proposes→app-reviews loop unless the app migrates too. Parked.

phases.title: Corpus → Postgres, step 1: move + verify the data
phases.summary: quran.db loaded into Postgres schema `corpus` in one transaction (UTF8-gated, repeatable, rolls back on failure) and verified exact on every row of every table. remote/src/corpus/. 11 tests. App/MCP untouched — still read SQLite.

phases.summary: plan_tiers table (runtime ladder); corpus_policy (public | signed_in | plan ≥ tier, default plan ≥ pro); translation_access (per-translation tier, locked ones omitted). Migration 0006, remote/src/{plans,corpus-access,access-cli}.ts. Proven end-to-end through the real app on real data.

phases.summary: DONE: content (chapters, verses in every script, words, neighbours, nav filters, translations) at remote /corpus/*, async twin of server/src/content.ts — corpus:parity: 7,152 answers identical to SQLite. decisions.decision: The corpus (quran.db) stays local; never hosted on the cloud.
decisions.why: 150 MB of static reference data; hosting it means re-implementing the whole corpus query layer against Postgres.

decisions.decision: Move the corpus to Postgres (the maintainer's call), in two steps: first move and verify the data, then port the readers.
decisions.why: Staged so nothing breaks: step 1 is additive and reversible (a separate `corpus` schema; the app keeps reading SQLite). The heavy, risky part — async-porting the query layer — is isolated in step 2 and can be proven with the existing parity suite. Whether cloud corpus reads are free or plan-gated is not yet decided (the principle so far: reading the Qur'an stays free).

decisions.decision: Community data is read live from the remote, never mirrored into research.db.
decisions.why: Mirroring puts it on the reader's disk, which makes it un-gateable. Live + gated is the enforceable design.

decisions.decision: Moderator review and maintainer establish are role-gated but NOT plan-gated.
decisions.why: The community's staff run it; charging them to moderate is counter-productive. One-line change if revisited.

decisions.decision: MCP stays local and free for now.
decisions.why: Corpus can't move to cloud; full cloud research reverses local-first and breaks the review loop. Monetization is already complete via the community layer.

decisions.decision: plan is a separate axis from role.
decisions.why: A moderator on the free plan can still moderate; a paying reader isn't automatically a researcher. Independent concerns.

decisions.decision: The plan ladder is a table, not code (maintainer's request: student/researcher/scholar-style tiers).
decisions.why: Tiers change with the business; a table lets the maintainer add or re-rank them with no deploy. Gates compare ranks, so a new tier slots in without touching any gate.

decisions.decision: Reading the cloud corpus is guarded by a runtime policy (public | signed_in | plan ≥ tier); default plan ≥ pro.
decisions.why: Maintainer's call: gated by default, but the admin can make reading free — or require only a sign-in — at any time. Fails closed if the setting is missing.

decisions.decision: A translation above the caller's tier is omitted from results, not refused.
decisions.why: One verse carries many translations; refusing the whole verse for one locked translation would be wrong. GET /corpus-access says what's locked so the app can offer the upgrade.

glossary.locally established: A form meaning YOU established, in your own research.db. Dated, yours, never overwritten.
glossary.globally established: The reading moderators accepted as the group's agreed meaning. Lives on the cloud.
glossary.dissent: A recorded disagreement with a globally established reading, preserved not resolved.
glossary.divergence (⚖): A form you established whose meaning differs from the group's. Computed live on the remote now.
glossary.claim: One author's reading of one subject (form or root); versions are that author's revisions; content-addressed id.
glossary.plan / planActive: The billing axis. planActive = paid rung AND not lapsed. The one flag the app gates on.
glossary.requireRole / requirePlan: The two Hono middlewares that gate a route: allowed-to vs paid-for.
